attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra


/-! ## The theta generator seed and the `lm:ctn` clauses -/

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π] {a : ℕ}

/-- **A theta generator seed for a submodule `K ⊆ H⁰(𝒪(Θᵃ))`** (worksheet §3.4.1): at
every point `z` of the relative curve, a pinned chart side containing `z`, a basic-open
neighbourhood piece `D(h z)` of the chart, and a global section `sec z ∈ K` — the
candidate local generator.  The two `lm:ctn` clauses on a seed are
`ThetaGeneratorSeed.IsGenerator`. -/
structure ThetaGeneratorSeed (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    [Algebra k R] (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π] (a : ℕ)
    (K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)) : Type u where
  /-- The pinned chart side of the piece at `z`. -/
  side : relCurve C R → Bool
  /-- The basic-open generator of the piece at `z`. -/
  h : ∀ z : relCurve C R, Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π (side z))
  /-- The point lies in its piece. -/
  mem_basicOpen : ∀ z : relCurve C R, z ∈ (relCurve C R).basicOpen (h z)
  /-- The candidate local generator at `z`. -/
  sec : relCurve C R → relThetaSections C R π a
  /-- The candidate generators are drawn from `K`. -/
  sec_mem : ∀ z, sec z ∈ K

namespace ThetaGeneratorSeed

variable {K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)} (D : ThetaGeneratorSeed C R π a K)

/-- The neighbourhood piece at `z`: the basic open `D(h z)` of the pinned chart. -/
noncomputable def piece (z : relCurve C R) : (relCurve C R).Opens :=
  (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h z)

lemma mem_piece (z : relCurve C R) : z ∈ D.piece z := D.mem_basicOpen z

lemma piece_le (z : relCurve C R) : D.piece z ≤ relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z) :=
  (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (D.h z)

/-- The pieces are affine (basic opens of the affine pinned charts). -/
lemma isAffineOpen_piece (z : relCurve C R) : IsAffineOpen (D.piece z) :=
  (isAffineOpen_relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z)).basicOpen (D.h z)

/-- **Flatness of the piece sections over the test ring** (the (iii)⟹(i) licence). -/
theorem flat_sections_piece (z : relCurve C R) :
    Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z) :=
  flat_sections_basicOpen R (isAffineOpen_relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z))
    (flat_sections_relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z)) (D.h z)

/-- **The candidate local equation at `z`**: the side component of the chosen generator,
restricted to the piece. -/
noncomputable def eqn (z : relCurve C R) : Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z) :=
  relThetaResSide a (D.side z) (D.piece_le z) (D.sec z)

/-- **The `lm:ctn` clauses on a seed** (Kleiman (ii)⟹(iii) packaged as its output, plus
the fibrewise-regularity input of (iii)⟹(i)):

* `dvd` — the chosen generator generates the subsheaf `K·𝒪` on its piece: the side
  component of every element of `K` is a multiple of the equation (the Nakayama
  neighbourhood clause, produced fibrewise by the P-fib achiever +
  `exists_fibrewise_tmul_ne_zero_of_projective`);
* `fibre_regular` — the equation is a nonzerodivisor in every residue-field fibre of
  every basic sub-open of the piece (produced by P-fib: the fibre of the equation is a
  nonzero section of an integral curve over `κ(p)`).

Both clauses are stated relative to the test ring only, so the DD-4 base-field-transport
seam moves a single boundary (spec-dd-r §7 risk 2). -/
structure IsGenerator : Prop where
  dvd : ∀ (z : relCurve C R) ⦃ψ : relThetaSections C R π a⦄, ψ ∈ K →
    relThetaResSide a (D.side z) (D.piece_le z) ψ ∈ Ideal.span {D.eqn z}
  fibre_regular : ∀ (z : relCurve C R) (p : PrimeSpectrum R)
      (f : Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z)),
    ((relCurve C R).resHom ((relCurve C R).basicOpen_le f) (D.eqn z) ⊗ₜ[R]
        (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) ∈
      nonZeroDivisors
        (Γ(relCurve C R, (relCurve C R).basicOpen f) ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField)

variable {D}

/-!
# Finite-adaptation extraction: every local-equation system has a chart adaptation
(`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §3 stage (d))

Every `LocalEquations` system `d` on the relative curve `C_R = relCurve C R` refines to a
finite chart adaptation `DivisorAdaptation C R π d` (`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §1a): the two
pinned charts `V₀ᴿ`, `V₁ᴿ` are affine, so the DAT-1 (1f) affine-refinement engine
(`IsAffineOpen.exists_finite_basicOpen_refinement` in
`AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.GluedSheafExtraction`)
produces, for each chart, a finite basic-open family subordinated to `d.cover` at anchor
points, with a partition of unity. Reindexing each chart family through `Fintype.equivFin`
gives the `Fin`-indexed `FinCoverData`; the equations are the restrictions of `d`'s
equations at the anchors (comparison unit `1`), regular by `d.regular` through the
refinement subordination.

The **certificate** (`DivisorAdaptation.IsCertified`) is deliberately NOT part of the
extraction: an adaptation always exists, whereas the colength certificate is an extra
finiteness/flatness hypothesis on `d` (the object of DD-1c's field dictionary and DAT-B's
coverage step, which supply it separately).

* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_divisorAdaptation` — the extraction: `Nonempty
  (DivisorAdaptation C R π d)` for every `d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations`.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
variable (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsAffineHom π]

/-- **Finite-adaptation extraction** (`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §3 stage (d), the DAT-1 (1f)
pattern): every local-equation system on the relative curve refines to a finite chart
adaptation. The two pinned charts are affine, so on each the affine-refinement engine
produces a finite basic-open family subordinated to `d.cover` at anchor points with a
partition of unity; the equations are the anchor equations of `d` restricted to the pieces
(comparison unit `1`), regular through the subordination. The colength certificate is a
separate hypothesis and is not produced here. -/
theorem exists_divisorAdaptation (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) :
    Nonempty (DivisorAdaptation C R π d) := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨ι₀, _, f₀, an₀, b₀, hsub₀, hpart₀⟩ :=
    (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C R (fiberTwoCover π)).exists_finite_basicOpen_refinement d.cover
  obtain ⟨ι₁, _, f₁, an₁, b₁, hsub₁, hpart₁⟩ :=
    (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C R (fiberTwoCover π)).exists_finite_basicOpen_refinement d.cover
  set e₀ : Fin (Fintype.card ι₀) ≃ ι₀ := (Fintype.equivFin ι₀).symm with he₀
  set e₁ : Fin (Fintype.card ι₁) ≃ ι₁ := (Fintype.equivFin ι₁).symm with he₁
  -- the `Fin`-indexed cover data
  set D : FinCoverData C R π :=
    { m₀ := Fintype.card ι₀
      m₁ := Fintype.card ι₁
      h₀ := fun j => f₀ (e₀ j)
      h₁ := fun j => f₁ (e₁ j)
      a₀ := fun j => b₀ (e₀ j)
      a₁ := fun j => b₁ (e₁ j)
      partition₀ := (Equiv.sum_comp e₀ (fun i => b₀ i * f₀ i)).trans hpart₀
      partition₁ := (Equiv.sum_comp e₁ (fun i => b₁ i * f₁ i)).trans hpart₁ } with hD
  -- the anchor of each piece and its subordination to a member of `d.cover`
  set pt : D.index → relCurve C R :=
    Sum.elim (fun j => an₀ (e₀ j)) (fun j => an₁ (e₁ j)) with hpt
  have hle : ∀ j : D.index, D.pieces j ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j) := by
    rintro (j | j)
    · exact hsub₀ (e₀ j)
    · exact hsub₁ (e₁ j)
  exact ⟨DivisorAdaptation.ofAnchors D
    (fun j => ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (hle j)).op).hom (d.eqn (pt j)))
    pt hle (fun _ => 1) (fun _ => by rw [Units.val_one, one_mul])⟩

end AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

/-! ## The flatness ladder: section rings of basic opens are flat over the test ring -/

section BasicOpenFlat

variable (K : Type u) [CommRing K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (.of K))]

/-- **Flatness descends to basic opens**: for an affine open `V` with `Γ(X, V)` flat over
the base ring `K`, the section ring of any basic open `D(f) ⊆ V` is flat over `K` —
`Γ(X, D(f))` is a localization of `Γ(X, V)` (`IsAffineOpen.isLocalization_basicOpen`),
localizations are flat, and flatness composes along the scalar tower
`K → Γ(X, V) → Γ(X, D(f))`. -/
theorem flat_sections_basicOpen {V : X.Opens} (hV : IsAffineOpen V)
    (hflat : Module.Flat K Γ(X, V)) (f : Γ(X, V)) :
    Module.Flat K Γ(X, X.basicOpen f) := by
  haveI := hflat
  haveI := hV.isLocalization_basicOpen f
  haveI : Module.Flat Γ(X, V) Γ(X, X.basicOpen f) :=
    IsLocalization.flat _ (Submonoid.powers f)
  haveI : IsScalarTower K Γ(X, V) Γ(X, X.basicOpen f) :=
    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun r =>
      (X.overAlgebraMap_apply_res K (homOfLE (X.basicOpen_le f)).op r).symm
  exact Module.Flat.trans K Γ(X, V) Γ(X, X.basicOpen f)

end BasicOpenFlat

/-! ## Section-level and unit-ratio consequences of germwise regularity -/

section GermRegular

variable {X : Scheme.{u}}

/-- A section all of whose germs are nonzerodivisors is a nonzerodivisor
(sections of a sheaf inject into the product of their germs). -/
theorem sections_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_forall_germ {W : X.Opens} {s : Γ(X, W)}
    (hreg : ∀ (y : X) (hy : y ∈ W),
      (X.presheaf.germ W y hy).hom s ∈ nonZeroDivisors (X.presheaf.stalk y)) :
    s ∈ nonZeroDivisors Γ(X, W) := by
  rw [mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff_right]
  intro t ht
  apply TopCat.Presheaf.section_ext X.sheaf W t 0
  intro y hy
  rw [map_zero]
  have key : (X.presheaf.germ W y hy).hom t * (X.presheaf.germ W y hy).hom s = 0 := by
    rw [← map_mul, ht, map_zero]
  exact (mul_right_mem_nonZeroDivisors_eq_zero_iff (hreg y hy)).mp key

/-- **Mutual divisibility against a germwise-regular section is a unit ratio**: if
`s = c₁ · t` and `t = c₂ · s` with every germ of `s` a nonzerodivisor, then `c₁` is a
unit, so `s = u · t` — the ratio-unit engine of the local-generator construction. -/
theorem exists_unit_mul_of_mutual_dvd {W : X.Opens} {s t c₁ c₂ : Γ(X, W)}
    (hreg : ∀ (y : X) (hy : y ∈ W),
      (X.presheaf.germ W y hy).hom s ∈ nonZeroDivisors (X.presheaf.stalk y))
    (h₁ : s = c₁ * t) (h₂ : t = c₂ * s) :
    ∃ u : Γ(X, W)ˣ, s = (u : Γ(X, W)) * t := by
  have hzero : (1 - c₁ * c₂) * s = 0 := by
    rw [sub_mul, one_mul, mul_assoc, ← h₂, ← h₁, sub_self]
  have hone : c₁ * c₂ = 1 := by
    have h := (mul_right_mem_nonZeroDivisors_eq_zero_iff
      (sections_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_forall_germ hreg)).mp hzero
    rwa [sub_eq_zero, eq_comm] at h
  exact ⟨Units.mkOfMulEqOne c₁ c₂ hone, h₁⟩

end GermRegular

/-! ## The pinned chart of a side and the side-uniform theta components -/

section Sides

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
variable (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π]

/-- The pinned chart of a side: `V₀ᴿ` for `false`, `V₁ᴿ` for `true`. -/
noncomputable def relPinnedChart : Bool → (relCurve C R).Opens
  | false => (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
  | true => (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁

@[simp]
lemma relPinnedChart_false :
    relPinnedChart C R π false = (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ := rfl

@[simp]
lemma relPinnedChart_true :
    relPinnedChart C R π true = (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ := rfl

/-- Both pinned charts are affine. -/
lemma isAffineOpen_relPinnedChart (b : Bool) : IsAffineOpen (relPinnedChart C R π b) := by
  cases b
  · exact relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C R (fiberTwoCover π)
  · exact relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C R (fiberTwoCover π)

/-- **Flatness of the pinned chart sections over the test ring**: `Γ(C_R, Vᵢᴿ)` is the
free base change `R ⊗[k] Γ(C, Vᵢ)` (`free_relSections`), hence flat. -/
theorem flat_sections_relPinnedChart (b : Bool) :
    Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b) := by
  cases b
  · haveI : Module.Free R Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π false) :=
      free_relSections C R (fiberChart₀ π)
        (isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen π 0).isCompact
        (isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen π 0).isQuasiSeparated
    exact Module.Flat.of_free
  · haveI : Module.Free R Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π true) :=
      free_relSections C R (fiberChart₁ π)
        (isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen π 1).isCompact
        (isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen π 1).isQuasiSeparated
    exact Module.Flat.of_free

`Picard/FibrewiseRegular` (fibrewise-regular + flat ⟹ regular) and
`Picard/FlatCokernel` (regular + flat quotient ⟹ regular after any base change):

> nonzerodivisor in every residue-field fibre `B ⊗[R] κ(p)`, then the quotient
> `B ⧸ (f)` is **flat** over `R`.

(`references/kleiman-picard-src/kleiman-picard.tex` 1786–1815): the paper's
`Tor₁(B/(f), κ) = 0` computation is replaced by the ideal criterion of flatness plus the
Noetherian ideal-division engine already underlying `FibrewiseRegular`. Concretely, for
`Q = coker φ` of an endomorphism `φ` of a flat module `M`, injectivity of the canonical
map `I ⊗ Q → Q` is chased through the right-exact ladder `I ⊗ M → I ⊗ Q` using only

* injectivity of `I ⊗ M → M` (flatness of `M`, `iff_lift_lsmul_comp_subtype_injective`),
* the **ideal-division property** `φ x ∈ I·M ⟹ x ∈ I·M` — which over a Noetherian `R` is

  flat colon lemma) as `Module.Flat.injective_of_forall_rTensor_residueField_injective`,
  here exposed as the public `Module.Flat.mem_smul_top_of_apply_mem_smul_top`.

No `Tor`, no local criterion of flatness, no finiteness hypothesis on `B`.

* `Module.Flat.mem_smul_top_of_apply_mem_smul_top` — the ideal-division engine
  (fibrewise-injective endomorphism of a flat module divides ideal memberships);
* `Module.Flat.of_surjective_exact_of_forall_mem_smul_top` — flatness of a cokernel from
  the ideal-division property (no Noetherian hypothesis);
* `Module.Flat.of_surjective_exact_of_forall_rTensor_residueField_injective` — the

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyFieldSurj
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyPullbackGlued

/-!
# Fibre rank of the Cech difference kernel from divisor degree

The pulled adaptation over a field has glued module equal to the kernel of the pulled
Cech difference.  Delta naturality transports this kernel to the base change of the
original difference map.  The field certificate constructed from divisor degree then
computes its dimension.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite TensorProduct
open Module (finrank)

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
variable {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K] [Algebra R K] [IsScalarTower k R K]
variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom pi]
variable [IsIntegral (relCurve C K)]
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [QuasiCompact (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]

namespace DivisorAdaptation

variable {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations} (A : DivisorAdaptation C R pi d)

omit [Algebra k K] [IsScalarTower k R K] [IsIntegral (relCurve C K)]
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [QuasiCompact (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] in
/-- The base-change and algebra-tensor spellings of the Cech difference have the same
kernel. -/
lemma ker_delta_baseChange_eq_ker_lTensor :
    LinearMap.ker ((A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight).baseChange K) =
      LinearMap.ker (AlgebraTensorModule.lTensor K K (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight)) := by
  ext x
  rw [LinearMap.mem_ker, LinearMap.mem_ker]
  rfl

set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
-- The proof elaborates the pulled adaptation and both product base-change equivalences.
set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 400000 in
/-- If the pulled local-equation divisor has degree `n`, then the fibre kernel of the
original Cech difference map has dimension `n`.  This is the exact `hdim` shape used by
`DivisorAdaptation.isCertified_of_kernel_spanning`. -/
theorem finrank_ker_delta_baseChange_eq_of_pulled_degree {n : Nat}
    (hproj : forall j : A.index, Module.Projective R (A.colength j))
    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg K
      (Scheme.presentationDivisor K
        ((A.pulledEquations K hproj).presentation)) = (n : Int)) :
    Module.finrank K
      (LinearMap.ker ((A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight).baseChange K)) = n := by
  let eMap := Submodule.equivMapOfInjective
    (A.chartProdBaseChange K).toLinearMap
    (A.chartProdBaseChange K).injective
    (LinearMap.ker (AlgebraTensorModule.lTensor K K (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight)))
  let e :
      LinearMap.ker ((A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight).baseChange K) ≃ₗ[K]
        A.pulledGluedSubmodule K :=
    (LinearEquiv.ofEq _ _ (A.ker_delta_baseChange_eq_ker_lTensor (K := K))).trans
      (eMap.trans (LinearEquiv.ofEq _ _ (A.map_ker_lTensor_delta K)))
  have hfr := ((A.pullback K hproj).isCertified_of_deg hdeg).finrank_glued
  change Module.finrank K (A.pulledGluedSubmodule K) = n at hfr
  rw [LinearEquiv.finrank_eq e]
  exact hfr

end DivisorAdaptation

end AlgebraicGeometry

## Verdict

The reduction in `DivSchemeCertZarSep.lean` is mathematically sound, but its hypothesis is **not achievable in the generic case, and provably so**: `hsep` forces the divisor support to avoid the overlap of the two pinned charts, which is a strong restriction on `d` that no refinement of the cover can repair. The repo already records this exact fact — for the field case — and the field endgame was *rewritten to avoid separation for this reason*:

`/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivisorFamilyFieldSurj.lean:33-38`:

> "**full support-separation is in fact unachievable when a support point lies in the overlap of the two pinned charts** (each chart's partition forces its pieces to cover the whole chart, so such a point lies in one piece of *each* chart)."

### (a) The no-go, precisely

Unconditional implication (provable from lemmas already in the file set, ~15 lines):

`hsep ⟹ d.supportLocus ∩ (V₀ ⊓ V₁) = ∅`.

Proof: let `z ∈ supp ∩ V₀ ∩ V₁`. `FinCoverData.cover₀` (`DivisorFamily.lean:199`) gives a chart-0 piece `i = inl i₀ ∋ z`; `cover₁` (`DivisorFamily.lean:204`) gives a chart-1 piece `j = inr j₀ ∋ z`; `i ≠ j` since `Sum.inl ≠ Sum.inr`. By `DivisorAdaptation.isUnit_germ_eqn_iff` (`SupportTube.lean:245`) the germs of both `eqn i`, `eqn j` at `z` are non-units, i.e. lie in `m_z`. So `ovlIdeal i j ≠ ⊤` (evaluate `1 = a·res f_i + b·res f_j` at the germ), so `ovlColength i j` is not subsingleton. Contradiction.

Consequences for your two sub-questions:

- **(i) No.** You cannot have one support-meeting piece per chart whose overlap misses the support, whenever the shared support point sits in `V₀ ⊓ V₁`. Both charts' partitions of unity force *every* point of `V₀ ⊓ V₁` into a chart-0 piece **and** a chart-1 piece simultaneously, and that pair is off-diagonal. Conversely, when the support does miss `V₀ ⊓ V₁` you never need two support-meeting pieces: the trivial cover `m₀ = m₁ = 1`, `h₀ = h₁ = 1` is legal `FinCoverData` (`partition₀ : 1*1 = 1`, `Scheme.basicOpen_one`), pieces `{V₀, V₁}`, one off-diagonal overlap `V₀ ⊓ V₁`.
- **(ii) Yes, but only for a thin family of divisors.** `V₀ \ V₁ = π⁻¹({[1:0]})` — a single fibre of `π` (`fiberTwoCover` at `Cohomology/RigidEngine4Relative.lean:75`; the "supported on `V₀ ∖ V₁` (the fiber of `π` over `[1:0]`)" reading is `RiemannRoch/FLVFiberToolkit.lean:290-292`, with `fiberWeilDivisor_coeffAt_of_mem_chart₁` at `:311` as the landed "support avoids `V₁`" lemma). So separation is achievable exactly for `d` with `supp d ⊆ π⁻¹({[1:0], [0:1]})` — divisors confined to two fixed fibres of `π`. That is a finite-rank sublattice of divisors; `Pic^g` needs a `g`-dimensional family, and the seed's fibre divisor (`divUniversalSeedFibreDivisor`, `DivSchemeSeedUnivFields.lean:133`, the *unique* effective degree-`g` divisor cutting both fibre windows at `κ(p)`) is not fibre-confined. Multiples of `fiberWeilDivisor` are the cases that do satisfy it.

Two escape hatches that do **not** work: `supportLocus` is `DivEq`-invariant (it is the complement of `unitLocus`, `SupportTube.lean:101/131`), so you cannot re-spell `d`; and shrinking the base via the pointwise gate (`isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_certified_adaptation`, `DivSchemeCertZarPointwise.lean:162`) only deletes fibres — it cannot move a support point out of `V₀ ⊓ V₁` at a retained prime.

### (b) Sanity check: yes, it was too good to be true — and nothing moved into (c1)/rank

Under `hsep`, every one of your remaining obligations is already discharged or soft:

- `[Module.Flat R B]`, `B = Γ(pieces j)`: **free**, not hard. `FinCoverData.flat_sections_pieces` (`SupportTube.lean:226-234`) → `flat_sections_basicOpen` + `flat_sections_relPinnedChart` (`DivSchemeFamilySide.lean:53, 135`), the latter because `Γ(C_R, V_i) ≅ R ⊗_k Γ(C, V_i)` is *free*. - (c1) projectivity then needs only fibrewise regularity of `eqn j`, which is landed for seed adaptations: `divisorAdaptation_fibre_regular` (`DivSchemeAdaptationFibreRegular.lean:585`), from `IsGenerator.fibre_regular` (`DivSchemeFamily.lean`, `IsGenerator`).

The route is **not circular** — it is a correct theorem with a premise that is essentially always false in the lane.

### (c)/(4) The field case gives you nothing to generalize

- No `hsep`-style hypothesis is discharged anywhere over a ring. Grep over `AlgebraicJacobian/` finds **no consumer** of `gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated`, `subsingleton_ovlColength_of_sep`, `finrank_glued_eq_sum_of_separated`, `deg_divFamDivisor_of_separated`, `isCertified_of_separated`, or `forall_subsingleton_ovlColength_of_unique_support_piece` outside their defining files and doc-comments. The deviation is documented at `DivisorFamilyFieldSurj.lean:29-45` and `DivisorFamilyFieldEquiv.lean:36-53`.
- Over a field the escape works because every module is free (so (c1)-projective, (c3), (c4) are instances) — exactly the input a nonreduced `R` denies. The field template's *real* content, adaptation-independence of the glued rank via stalk-CRT, is what would have to be relativized; over a ring that is the flat-cokernel/kernel-spanning statement again.

## Bottom line

1. **Achievability:** `hsep` (hence the one-support-piece hypothesis) holds iff `supp d ∩ (V₀ ⊓ V₁) = ∅`, i.e. the divisor lives in the two vertical fibres `π⁻¹{[1:0],[0:1]}`. Achievable for fibre-type divisors (`fiberWeilDivisor` multiples), not for a general degree-`g` divisor or the universal seed's fibre divisor. Evidence: `DivisorFamily.lean:174-176, 199-207`; `SupportTube.lean:245`; `DivisorFamilyFieldSurj.lean:33-38`; `FLVFiberToolkit.lean:290-292, 311`.
2. **Remaining obligations under your reduction** (all soft, all landed or free): fibrewise regularity of the piece equation; `Module.Finite` of the colength from support-containment; fibrewise degree = `n`. The `[Module.Flat R B]` of the `SlicingFlat` keystone is free (piece sections are localizations of a *free* `R`-module); `[Module.Flat R A.ovlProd]` is derivable from (c1) under `hsep`.
3. **Where the hard content lives:** unchanged — in the flat-cokernel/kernel-spanning equivalence (`DivSchemeHighWindowSyzygy.lean:298`). Your reduction relocates it into the existence of a separated adaptation, which is a provable no-go for supports meeting the chart overlap, not a cheaper hypothesis.

    haveI : Subsingleton (A.colength j) :=

49	`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):
50	
51	- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
52	  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
53	  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
54	  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
55	  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
56	  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
57	  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
58	  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
59	  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
60	  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
61	  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
62	  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
63	- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
64	  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
65	  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
66	- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
67	  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
68	  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
69	  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
70	  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
71	  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
72	  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
73	- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
74	  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
75	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
76	  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
77	- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
78	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
79	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
80	- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
81	  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
82	  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.

101	## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)
102	
103	Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
104	The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:
105	
106	- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
107	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
108	  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
109	  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
110	- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
111	  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
112	  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
113	- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
114	  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).
115	
116	## One-shot discipline (important)
117	
118	This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
119	when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
120	(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
121	uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).
122	
123	## Pick the highest-value work
124	
125	Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
126	piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
127	infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
128	lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
129	you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.
130	
131	If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
132	task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
133	the objective is large. Leave a `"$HORIZON_BIN" task comment <task_id> --body …`
134	at each significant step. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
135	`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
136	`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
137	(it returns to the queue).
138	
139	## Fresh-context checkpoints
140	
141	The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
142	review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
143	checkpoints:
144	
145	- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
146	- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
147	- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
148	  clean/build result.
149	
150	Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
151	blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
152	is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
153	continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
154	when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
155	periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
156	terminal `done` claim.
157	
158	Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
159	multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
160	session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
161	before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
162	Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
163	If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
164	Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.
165	
166	## Warnings are work
167	
168	Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
169	warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
170	notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
171	the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
172	silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
173	address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
174	survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
175	why.
176	
177	Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
178	`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
179	or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
180	workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
181	record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
182	same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
183	issue rather than repeated no-op calls.
184	
185	## Do the work (Lean)
186	
187	For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
188	required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
189	`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
190	build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
191	LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
192	lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
193	configured final build covers the same files.
194	
195	**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
196	find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
197	afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
198	mathlib — query it:
199	
200	| You want | Use | Not |
201	|---|---|---|
202	| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
203	| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
204	| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
205	| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
206	| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
207	| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
208	| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |
209	
210	`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
211	its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
212	you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
213	existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
214	first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
215	back to grep.
216	
217	Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
218	specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.
219	
220	- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
221	- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
222	  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
223	- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
224	- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
225	  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
226	  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
227	  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
228	  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.
229	
230	## Read the other projects
231	
232	They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
233	often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
234	projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
235	import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
236	original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
237	the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.

239	## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)
240	
241	Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
242	(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
243	needs no permission.
244	
245	Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
246	spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
247	and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
248	standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
249	`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
250	`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
251	limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
252	or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
253	proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
254	its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.
255	
256	## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)
257	
258	Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
259	dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
260	`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
261	or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).
262	
263	Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
264	staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:
265	
266	- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
267	- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
268	  as **memory**.
269	
270	Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
271	`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
272	strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
273	archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
274	remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
275	that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
276	shorter. This pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.
277	
278	## Resuming after an interruption
279	
280	State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
281	cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
282	the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:
283	
284	- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
285	  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
286	  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
287	  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
288	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
289	- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
290	  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
291	  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
292	  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
293	- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
294	  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
295	  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
296	  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
297	  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
298	  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
299	  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
300	  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.
301	
302	## Final report (your last message)
303	
304	Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
305	session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
306	Recommended sections: `## Summary`, `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
307	`## Why I stopped`, `## Next` (keep at least `## Progress` and
308	`## Why I stopped`). In `## Progress`, one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
309	e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
310	stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
311	or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
312	dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
313	action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
314	not by itself a reason to stop.

317	
318	There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,

320	workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
